prerequisites: 836- Matemáticas I: Integration and derivation with one variable; Resolution of systems of equations; Calculation with complex numbers; Fourier series.
837- Matemáticas II: Resolution of systems of equations.
844- Matemáticas III: Curl, Vector calculus, Resolution of differential equations.
840- Mecánica: Conservative forces and potential energy. Non-conservative forces and work.

learning_outcomes.text: The student will know and be able to apply the general laws of electricity and magnetism.
The student will know and be able to use the concepts related to capacitance, electric current, and electromagnetic induction.
The student will know and be able to apply the general laws of direct current and alternating current electrical circuits.
The student will know the analysis of magnetic circuits and its application in the calculation of magnetic circuits of electrical machines.
The student will know and understand the creation of rotating magnetic fields.
The student will know, understand, and be able to apply the principles of basic electric generators and motors.
The student will know and understand the properties of electromagnetic waves.

syllabus_topics: Electric field. Electric potential. Introduction. Definition of field. Electric charges: electrification, properties, force and electric field. Charge distributions. Gauss's Law: Applications. Electric potential. Electric potential energy.
Dielectrics. Capacitance and capacitors. Conductors in an electrostatic field. Dielectrics in electric fields. Capacitor and capacitance. Capacitor association. Capacitor with dielectric.

Electric current. Current intensity and current density. Ohm's Law. Power supplied by an electric field and Joule effect. EMF. Power dissipated in a resistance and supplied by an EMF. Resistance association. Kirchhoff's Laws. Elementary analysis of direct current circuits.

Magnetic field. Magnetic field. Induction. Magnetic flux. Magnetic field created by a moving charge. Magnetic field created by a current element. Biot-Savart Law. Magnetic field of a current-carrying conductor. Magnetic field of a circular loop. Magnetic field of a solenoid. Ampere's Law and examples of Ampere's Law. Force on a moving charge. Force on a current-carrying conductor. Force between two parallel conductors (Ampere's). Force and torque on a rectangular coil.

Electromagnetic Induction. Electromotive force (due to motion). Faraday's Law. Lenz's Law. EMF on a conductor rotating in a magnetic field. EMF on an N-turn coil. Eddy currents. Mutual induction. Self-induction. Effect of self-induction upon circuit closing. Effect of self-induction upon EMF cancellation. Energy of a circuit with self-induction. Self-inductions in series.
Magnetic Properties. Origin of magnetic effects. Equivalent surface currents. Magnetic excitation. Magnetization. Susceptibility. Permeability. Ferromagnetism. Hysteresis and consequences.
Magnetic Circuits. Hopkinson's Law. Series magnetic circuit. Parallel magnetic circuit.

Application to Electrical Machines. General classification of Electrical Machines. General constitution of a Rotary Electrical Machine. MMF of simple coils and current layer. Induction wave in the air gap. Sinusoidal rotating MMF and field. EMF and torque in multiple excitation systems.

Elementary analysis of alternating current. Sinusoidal alternating current. Alternating current. Defining equations of elements: behavior of elements. Sinusoidal alternating current. Representation of voltage and current. R, C, and L circuits, capacitive and inductive reactances, phase shifts. Complex impedance and admittance. Power in sinusoidal alternating current. Sinusoidal alternating current circuits. Approximation to non-sinusoidal alternating current circuits.
Electromagnetic Waves. Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics. Maxwell's Equations.

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a Final Grade of at least 50% (5 out of 10) is required. Students must achieve a minimum of 35% of the final written exam grade to pass; otherwise, the final grade cannot exceed 4.5 out of 10. The score for observation techniques is based on active participation and evaluation of exercises and/or theoretical and/or practical questions posed in class. Attendance at the associated practical session is mandatory for a practical report to be evaluated.
